Reason: The CT images demonstrate small, well-defined nodules distributed along the peribronchovascular bundles and in the subpleural regions, particularly visible in the upper lung zones (Figure 1a), which is the classic radiological pattern for sarcoidosis. This distribution distinguishes it from the random pattern of miliary TB or the centrilobular pattern of inhalation diseases.
